Clairin Ti Punch

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

1 servingPrep 2 min

Clairin Ti Punch is a quintessential Haitian cocktail, a simple yet potent blend that embodies the spirit of the island. For Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa, this drink serves as a refreshing and traditional offering, honoring the agricultural bounty and the hard work of farmers. It's a perfect way to celebrate the harvest and share in the communal joy of the festival.

Ingredients

  • 2 ounces (60 ml) Clairin (Haitian unaged rum)
  • 1/4 fresh lime, cut into a small wedge or disc
  • 1-2 teaspoons cane sugar or cane syrup (agave nectar or simple syrup can be substituted)

Method

  1. Place the cane sugar or cane syrup at the bottom of a small, sturdy glass (like an Old Fashioned glass).
  2. Squeeze the lime wedge directly into the glass, ensuring some of the essential oils from the peel are released. Drop the squeezed lime wedge into the glass.
  3. Using a muddler or the back of a spoon, gently muddle the lime with the sugar/syrup for about 10-15 seconds to dissolve the sugar and release more lime oils.
  4. Pour the Clairin into the glass.
  5. Stir well until all ingredients are combined.
  6. Serve immediately. Traditionally, Ti Punch is served without ice, but you may add a single large ice cube if preferred.

Tips

  • For a more authentic experience, use raw cane sugar or a good quality cane syrup, which imparts a distinct flavor.
  • The key to a great Ti Punch is the fresh lime; don't skip muddling the peel to release its aromatic oils.
  • While traditionally served without ice, a single large ice cube can be added for those who prefer a slightly chilled and less potent sip.
